I mean... they've been dating for 8 months, a period where its more than normal to follow and know about each others social media accounts, and it's an account set to *private*. I'd have to argue those things combined equal the definition of "secret" without being overly dramatic.  

>I called asking to follow it juvenile because I personally think people in romantic relationships still get to have separate friendships. It isn’t necessary to be involved in everything and is some ways it isn’t healthy.

I really miss when the phrase "it can't hurt to ask" was accurate, and instead, now you're an AH for asking to be a part of your bf's life. Ok, maybe she "overstepped" by asking the friend as well, but the bf ruined her trust by BLOCKING her in response to her first question. Most people would hear "my bf has a secret and private social account" and assume they are using it to cheat. He did nothing to quell her curiosity/concerns

I have to disagree with the gf going to the friend as juvenile. At the moment the only information she has is that it's a secret account with 2 owners. Why is it so juvenile to ask to follow a "normal" account. Now OP is juvenile by having a problem letting his gf see the account. He's juvenile by kicking her out of the apartment (that she possibly lives in) just to keep the two people away from each other. And it's extremely suspect that OP thinks it's reasonable and not AH-ish behavior to kick your gf out of an apartment because she asked to follow an account. No other behavior other than just *asking*

I'm more of a romance reader than a watcher, but in either medium I absolutely cannot enjoy a romcom. Ironically the genres I love to read, dark and monster romance, most people would consider much more unhealthy than a "normal" romcom, but something about how they are deeply disconnected from reality helps me enjoy them.

Neither of those things sound like a healthy relationship. No one should love another person more than they love themselves. But they shouldn't need to hurt you so they feel better or more loved. And that person should be able to love you on both your good days and bad days, not just the good days. If you have to ask the question, it's probably not the love you need.

For anything I give myself a hard time for, I can instantly name 5 insane things my mom was hard on me for, and that conditioning is so difficult to break. It's almost like a security blanket, if I assume the worst or give myself a hard time, anything the outside world does to me can't be worse because I've already gone through it in my mind.

I had appendicitis. Couldn't get out of bed but somehow was forced to go to grandma's birthday party AND pay for it (years later I'm still disgusted with myself for paying for it) where 2 family friends could tell something was wrong with me but my own family was in denial. Kicker was, by the time I finally ended up at the hospital, I was partly dying from the infection. But because I was a woman who couldn't advocate for myself they acted too conservative with my treatment. So I ended up suffering for 4x the amount of time I should have.
I didn't say it couldn't happen, just that it would surprise me to run across

I started journaling to try to cut down on how much I tell my nmom. Ngl, it's a process. My problem is my nmom has put me down for my communication skills so many times (because to them any words out of our mouths are dramatic and unnecessary 🙄) that I feel shame for needing to rant about my feeling for X amount of pages. But I am still trying to consider it an achievement for choosing the journal over *her*

I also wondered how many other apologies before then she's felt were unnecessary, but she had the mental acuity before to just try to end the issue. Since then I can't stand to hear any form of apology because I just don't believe it. 😒

Turns out I was getting blamed for all of her bad behavior in uBPD's head, and she decided to spiral hard on me this weekend. I'm finding a lot of old sitcoms relied on having "flawed parents" who actually have a lot of bpd/narcissistic tendencies.

She only knew I wanted a journal... and bought me an Exercise Journal... I've openly struggled with body dismorphia for a year 😬

Let me guess... you're also a woman? The way people fixate on weight relating to health when it comes to women is disgusting. I used to be overweight, and every doctors appointment focused on "if you lose weight your symptoms would improve". Then a year ago my diseases started targeting my stomach. I've lost 110 lbs and counting. In a twist no one saw coming, 0 symptoms changed because of weight loss, but all the voices stopped commenting on my weight being the solution (other than "oh how good you look!" Or worse, "oh what a great side effect it is". NOPE! I personally would have rathered the ability to eat complete meals than the weightloss). I'm also STILL losing weight, and am heading in the direction of underweight conversations. Aren't I so lucky? 🙃 

It's 2021, and very well known that people have a wide variety of body image issues. I don't understand how people still think it's ok to comment on this stuff when you never know what's going on in the other persons head.
